vex

/VEKS/ - rhymes with checks · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Vex means to annoy or irritate.

The conference line's half-second echo vexed the negotiators into talking over one another for an hour.

Worked Example

The hotel's key cards vexed Mr. Osei all weekend — accepted at midnight, refused at one, and at two, inexplicably, his room-service menu opened the door.

Vex is old, small, and precise: a vexation buzzes at your patience without breaking it. The word can also color puzzles — a vexed question is one that nags — but the center is minor, persistent irritation. When patience actually gives out, this unit's exasperate is waiting.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

irk: To irk is to rub someone the wrong way, quietly — a low-grade annoyance the irked person may never even mention. To vex is a shade sharper and far more persistent: a vexation keeps buzzing at the patience and insists on being noticed. An irked person shrugs; a vexed one mutters.

nettle: To nettle is to sting someone's pride just enough to redden the temper — usually one sharp, personal poke, often a remark. To vex is less personal and more patient: small irritations, delays, and riddles that nag at the attention over time. Nettle stings once; vexation keeps buzzing.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

soothe: to smooth irritation away

please: to give simple satisfaction

Where it sits · how deeply it eats at patience — bother → vex → infuriate

bother vs. vex: Bother is milder than vex — a fly at the picnic, shooed and forgotten.

infuriate vs. vex: Infuriate is far stronger than vex: vexation prickles at your patience, while fury has already burned through it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — vex

Root — vex: to shake, to agitate (Latin vexare)

Put it together

Put it together: There is nothing to peel off here: vex is Latin vexare, 'to shake, to jolt, to harass,' compressed to three letters. The shaking survives in miniature — whatever vexes you gives your patience one small, repeated jostle.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: Latin vexare produced vex and its own noun vexation, and then stopped; no other common English word shares the root. The similar-sounding convex is unrelated — it comes from vehere, 'to carry.'

Strength Check

Word Choice

neutral / slightly formal

Vex suits small, persistent irritations and the faintly old-fashioned sentence — squeaks, delays, riddles that nag. Annoy is the plain modern word; irk and nettle are its quieter cousins. When the irritation has worn patience through, reach for this unit's exasperate instead.
